analysis.investment_thesis: CLN Energy fails nearly every quantitative Graham filter: incorporated only in 2019, it lacks the 5-year earnings record I require, and at P/E 25.4 with an implied P/B near 3.5, the price offers no margin of safety. This is an EV-story IPO priced for growth, not a proven enterprise trading below intrinsic value.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 72.6% signals skin-in-the-game and reduces float-driven speculation.
ROE of 13.7% is respectable if sustainable — above cost of equity.
FII participation at 12.6% indicates some institutional diligence has occurred.
key_risks: Only 6 years old (founded 2019) — no multi-year earnings track record to value.
P/E 25.4 and implied P/B ~3.5 (P/E × ROE) blow past my <15 and <1.5 ceilings.
Graham Number (~INR 205) is roughly half the market price of INR 406 — zero margin of safety.
red_flags: Recent listing / IPO — seller (promoter + bankers) knows more than the buyer.
ROCE (12.25%) is below ROE (13.7%), hinting at financial leverage boosting returns.
Lithium-ion / EV components is a capital-intensive, commoditizing industry with unproven moats.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my strict quantitative lens, CLN Energy is disqualified before we even debate the business. I require at least five consecutive years of positive earnings; a company incorporated in 2019 cannot possibly satisfy that. The price of INR 406 against a P/E of 25.4 implies EPS of ~INR 16, and with ROE of 13.7% the book value per share is roughly INR 117 — giving a P/B near 3.5x and a Graham Number of only ~INR 205. The market is paying nearly double what my formula permits, with none of the cushion that protects against error or misfortune.

The narrative — lithium-ion batteries and EV powertrains — is precisely the sort of seductive growth story Mr. Market prices enthusiastically and later regrets. ROCE (12.25%) trailing ROE (13.7%) suggests leverage is doing work, and at a INR 296 Cr market cap this is a small, unseasoned enterprise in a capital-intensive, rapidly-evolving industry. I see no dividend yield, no liquidity data, no balance-sheet strength disclosed here that could compensate. Defensive and enterprising investor alike should pass; speculators are welcome to it.
